newsitem.title: USA: Commodore Applied says venture names head.
newsitem.headline: Commodore Applied says venture names head.

text.p: Commodore Applied Technologies Inc said Wednesday that retired Maj. Gen. Gerald Watson had been named president and chief executive of Teledyne-Commodore LLC, a joint venture formed to apply the solvated electron technology process to the destruction of chemical warfare weapons and agents.

The joint venture is between the company's subsidiary, Commodore Government Environmental Technologies Inc and Teledyne Environmental Inc, which is affiliated with the Teledyne Brown Engineering division of Teledyne Industries Inc .
Watson has been the U.S. Army's chief chemical officer. In his last posting before retiring in 1992, he was director of the Defense Nuclear Agency.
The joint venture was formed in August.
